Landing.heroBody: TIAI is a Texas nonprofit focused on AI education and applied research. We are developing an education model that brings AI into subject learning, project work and assessment, helping learners build knowledge, sound judgment and capabilities they can demonstrate.
Landing.aboutBody: Learners need support to apply classroom knowledge to open-ended problems, evaluate AI-generated work and explain their own contribution. Our AI-native education model connects these needs across curriculum, projects, assessment and preparation for professional practice.
Landing.aboutPoint1Body: Build subject knowledge through guided study, AI-assisted exploration and independent practice. Learning goals define when to use AI, how to check its output and what students must understand for themselves.
Landing.aboutPoint2Body: Frame a problem, investigate evidence and develop a solution within defined user needs, time and resource limits. Record decisions, test results and revisions so the work can be reviewed.
Landing.aboutPoint3Body: Combine project demonstrations, reproducible tests and oral explanations. Make each learner’s reasoning, AI use and individual contribution visible, with feedback guiding the next round of practice.
Landing.program1Body: Study how AI systems learn, build applications and evaluate their reliability. Proposed projects connect models and data with practical questions and responsible use.
Landing.program2Body: Develop foundations in programming, algorithms and systems. Use AI throughout software development while learning to explain, test and maintain the resulting work.
Landing.program3Body: Connect data and AI with organizational needs. Investigate workflows, build analysis tools and evaluate the quality and usefulness of the results.
Landing.partnershipBody: We welcome discussions with universities and colleges about curriculum, project-based learning and student support. Potential collaborations begin with agreed educational goals, clear responsibilities and the institution’s approval process.
Landing.partnershipStep1: Identify learner needs, intended capabilities and the scope of a possible collaboration.
Landing.partnershipStep2: Develop a curriculum, project and assessment plan for institutional review.
Landing.partnershipStep3: After agreements and approvals, define a pilot and review the learning evidence before considering expansion.
Landing.partnershipPoint1: Academic foundations and AI-supported learning activities
Landing.partnershipPoint2: Project briefs, mentoring and student learning support
Landing.partnershipPoint3: Assessment criteria, individual contribution records and portfolios
Landing.partnershipPoint4: Applied research questions and evaluation of educational practice
Landing.partnershipGovernanceBody: Any collaboration would require a formal agreement. Academic approvals, admission, credit, transcripts and degree conferral remain with duly authorized institutions. No specific partnership or accredited program is announced here.
Landing.facultyBody: We invite educators, researchers and practitioners to discuss contributions to curriculum, mentoring and assessment. Specific roles and terms depend on the project and a separate agreement.
Landing.facultyBenefit1Body: Connect subject foundations with responsible AI use and explicit learning goals.
Landing.facultyBenefit2Body: Help learners define problems, test approaches and explain technical decisions.
Landing.facultyBenefit3Body: Develop ways to review project quality, independent understanding and individual contributions.
Landing.facultyBenefit4Body: Explore questions in AI-supported learning and domain applications through carefully scoped studies.
Landing.insight1Body: How can AI support practice and feedback while strengthening independent understanding?
Landing.insight2Body: Which project records, tests and explanations show what a learner can do?
Landing.insight3Body: How can academic foundations inform useful work in industry, research and public service?

Landing.registryLine6: Principal Office: 5900 Balcones Drive, Suite 100, Austin, TX 78731
Landing.contactBody: Contact us about learning plans, university collaboration or contributions to teaching and research. We will explain the current scope and relevant next steps.

Landing.aboutPoint4Body: Build a portfolio that shows technical work, collaboration, communication and responsible judgment. These capabilities support further study and career development; admission and hiring decisions belong to the relevant institutions and employers.
Landing.programsBody: Our planning connects AI, computing and information systems with undergraduate preparation, master’s preparation and potential university-led master’s collaborations. Each area brings together foundational study, applied projects and evidence of learning.
Landing.programsStatus: These are proposed areas for development and discussion. Delivery, enrollment and any university collaboration depend on confirmed arrangements and applicable approvals. TIAI does not award degrees or guarantee credit, transfer, admission, employment or accreditation.

Faculty.heroBody: TIAI is building a distributed network of AI educators, researchers, and industry practitioners to co-deliver high-quality education programs across partner institutions.
Faculty.role1Body: Teach courses within accredited partner college programs. All instructors are credentialed and appointed through institutional processes.
Faculty.role2Body: Contribute to course design, learning outcomes, and industry alignment without a full teaching commitment.
Faculty.role3Body: Collaborate on applied AI research and educational case studies. Formal attribution provided.
Faculty.benefit2: Priority access to paid teaching opportunities
Faculty.benefit4: Network of AI practitioners and educators
Faculty.ctaBody: Submit your background and interest area. Our academic team will follow up within 5 business days.

About.heroBody: Texas Institute of Artificial Intelligence is a Texas nonprofit developing an AI-native approach to education. Our focus is on connecting academic foundations, applied work and evidence of individual capability.
About.missionBody: Help learners use knowledge and AI responsibly in further study, professional practice and research. We aim to make the route from learning a concept to applying it, testing it and explaining the result clear and accessible.
About.modelBody: TIAI develops educational concepts and welcomes discussions about curriculum, projects and learning support. Undergraduate preparation, master’s preparation and university-led master’s collaborations are planning directions subject to formal agreements and approvals. TIAI does not award degrees or issue transcripts; admission, credit and qualifications remain the responsibility of authorized institutions.
About.reg1: Legal Name: Texas Institute of Artificial Intelligence

About.value1Body: Use guided study and independent practice to develop subject knowledge, research literacy and the ability to transfer ideas to unfamiliar problems.
About.value2Body: Learn to select tools, check evidence and recognize limitations. Take responsibility for the accuracy, ethics and consequences of the work.
About.value3Body: Show what each learner understands and contributes through project records, tests and explanations. Use feedback to build capability and a credible portfolio.

UniversityPartnerships.heroTitle: Build rigorous AI pathways with clear academic governance
UniversityPartnerships.heroBody: TIAI works with institutions on AI, computer science, mathematics, English, transfer, and pathway program design while preserving each institution's authority over admission, credit, records, and credentials.

models.title: Master's pathway preparation
models.body: Bridge coursework can help students from non-CS backgrounds prepare for graduate-level study in computing, data, and AI. Any admission decision remains with the receiving institution.

models.title: Conditional pathway support
models.body: TIAI can help design preparatory study in computing, mathematics, English, and AI foundations for institutions that choose to evaluate students through their own policies.

models.title: Undergraduate transfer readiness
models.body: Programs can support community college, 2+2, or transfer-oriented preparation where credit and articulation decisions remain under institutional control.

models.title: Curriculum and faculty development
models.body: TIAI can support joint curriculum development, instructor preparation, course licensing discussions, and quality review for AI education.

models.title: AI lab and applied research collaboration
models.body: Institutions and industry partners can explore applied AI education, AI agents, reliable AI, and workforce-aligned projects without overstating current research output.

models.title: International teaching center model
models.body: TIAI can help coordinate local teaching support and student services where governance, records, and credential decisions remain with authorized institutions.

responsibilities.title: TIAI can support
items: Program design and operational planning
Bridge curriculum in AI, CS, math, and English foundations
Instructor network development and teaching support
Student advising, progress monitoring, and learning support
Quality assurance reporting and continuous improvement

responsibilities.title: Partner institutions retain
items: Admission and enrollment decisions
Academic policy and curriculum approval
Credit, transcript, and degree authority
Instructor credential review where applicable
Compliance with accreditation and institutional standards

process: Clarify institutional goals, student profile, and target pathway.
Map TIAI support responsibilities against institutional governance requirements.
Pilot a limited, auditable program before broader expansion.
UniversityPartnerships.disclaimer: No page on this site should be read as a promise of admission, academic credit, transfer acceptance, financial aid, immigration outcome, or degree conferral. Those decisions belong to the authorized institutions and agencies responsible for them.

ForStudents.heroTitle: Build the foundations needed for AI, CS, and transfer pathways
ForStudents.heroBody: TIAI is designed for learners who need a serious bridge into computing, mathematics, AI practice, and institution-approved academic pathways.
fitItems: Students from non-CS backgrounds who need computing and math foundations before advanced AI study.
International students exploring U.S. undergraduate transfer or graduate preparation routes.
Learners who want project-based AI education without relying on unsupported degree or job guarantees.
Working professionals and recent graduates who need a structured path into applied AI skills.

pathItems.title: AI & Machine Learning
pathItems.body: Applied AI foundations, machine learning practice, model deployment, and responsible use.

pathItems.title: Computer Science Foundations
pathItems.body: Programming, algorithms, systems thinking, and software engineering preparation.

pathItems.title: Information Systems
pathItems.body: Data, business technology, databases, analytics, and organizational systems.

applicationItems: Submit your academic background, goals, and preferred pathway.
TIAI reviews fit and recommends a preparation path or next conversation.
If a partner institution is involved, admission, credit, and enrollment steps follow that institution's policies.
Students receive a clear explanation of what TIAI can support and what it cannot promise.
ForStudents.disclaimer: TIAI does not promise admission, transfer, credit recognition, visa approval, employment, or degree completion. Program outcomes depend on student performance and the policies of relevant institutions and agencies.
